This project addressed issues of… Show more The Catchers Curation organized an end-to-end art exhibition "Tale of the Exiled: Salvaged works from Art School Waste" to showcase abandoned artworks from New York City art schools. These orphan works of various genres and media were produced by visual art students. The artworks, discarded due to dilemmas in the art schools, the art world, and society in a capitalistic context, were exhibited in an inclusive and non-judgmental space in downtown Manhattan. This project addressed issues of sustainability and inclusivity by providing a forum for marginalized artists to share their stories. The exhibition inaugurated in November 2023. The possibility of recurring exhibitions in various locations welcomes abandoned artworks from around the world.​ As a PR & Finance Lead at The Catchers Curation, I managed 12 fundraising campaigns, secured sponsors through targeted outreach, and raised $800+ to fund the exhibition. Coordinating this campaign taught me how to bridge gaps between stakeholders, promote inclusivity, and create significant opportunities through innovative solutions. Several people I met on the team became my lifetime best friends. In addition, I built the exhibition's H5 website featuring interactive virtual tours and personalized art recommendations and initiated a digital marketplace connecting emerging artists with potential buyers with different audience segments including students, educators, activists, and the general public. (For more detailed information regarding this art exhibition, feel free to have a look at the 'Tales of the Abandoned.pdf' below:)) Show less

The token prediction patterns demonstrated at #GoogleResearch2024 Symposium last Thursday challenged my understanding of auto-regressive models. Watching their live demos, I was struck by how the computational demands varied drastically across different prediction tasks - a fundamental challenge that's rarely discussed but crucial for practical applications. Their work on locally calibrated data particularly resonated with me. The team showed how this approach not only improves flood forecasting accuracy but could revolutionize how we handle prediction tasks across domains. Seeing them achieve 7-day advance forecasts while maintaining local precision was impressive. What fascinated me most was their novel take on predictive attention models. The neuroscience session demonstrated how attention mechanisms could serve as reward models - an elegant solution that has implications far beyond their initial use case. This kind of cross-pollination of ideas, seeing how concepts from one field can unlock possibilities in another, is exactly why I love this field. The disease progression modeling using transformer architectures showed just how far we've come in handling temporal dependencies. Their success in integrating cell state predictions with sequential disease modeling points to exciting possibilities for early intervention. It was encouraging to see their work and achievements, as I've been exploring similar directions in my current project. 💡Grateful to have witnessed these technical breakthroughs firsthand. Looking forward to exploring these concepts further, especially the intersection of attention mechanisms and real-world applications. #MachineLearning #AIResearch #ComputationalModeling ...more

Join us for the grand opening of our captivating exhibition showcasing the abandoned art works and redefining the concept of "abandonment." 🎆 😀 Exhibition Descriptions & Details: By the end of each art school’s semester, there are piles after piles of student artworks thrown out into the trash, taken into the dumpster to be buried, burned, destroted. The Catchers collected more than a hundred and seventy of these pieces from the previous fall and spring semesters, some stright from the bins, others right before the works were collectively disposed by the art schools in which they are created. Some pieces were never intentionally “abandoned”, and we hope to find their creators through this exhibition; others we obtained consent from the artists for them to be displayed and their stories to be told. But the *Tale of the Abandoned* wants to convey more than just about the stories of the salvaged works; we hope to shine light on the concept of “abandonment” itself, to invite our dear audience to join us in the contemplation of abandonement: How and why does it come about? When do we notice what we abandon, and when do we not? When we abandon something, where does it go? Can we ever truly abandon anything at all? … The list of questions go on, and we want you to add on to it. About The Catchers Curation: The Catchers' Curation is a non-profit curatorial team established and built for this very art exhibition project, consisting of 37 full-time students from universities across the globe. We noticed the large amount of abandoned art in the School of Visual Arts and the other schools we attend, which includes Pratt Institute, Fashion Institute of Technology, The New School and more. The Catchers run on the passion we have for art, the care we hold for artists, and the curiosity we choose to navigate the world with. Brought together by a common wish to redeem the abandoned student artworks, we are striving to make our little exhibition become reality. ...more

Today was my last day as a Machine Learning Engineer Intern at Adobe. 🎈 Over the past few months, I worked on building an evaluation framework for AI agents: designing a system that mines an agent's real production failures, diagnoses what went wrong, and surfaces the root causes engineers can act on. I got to take it from a rough set of scripts all the way to a reusable framework, and see it start to extend to a second agent. I learned an enormous amount about system design, working with LLMs, and what it takes to build something others can actually rely on. What made it special was the team and the pace: working on fast-moving AI products, with new problems to dig into every week. I never stopped learning, and I always felt supported doing it. Add to that a culture that genuinely respects people's time, and it's hard to imagine a better place to spend a summer! Huge thanks to my mentor Sahil Khanna and my manager Jie L. r Jie L. for their guidance, patience, and for trusting me with real, meaningful work. I'm grateful to the whole team for making this such a rewarding few months! Excited for what's next! 🚀

Tetrix , a NYC-based provider of an AI investment platform for limited partners in alternative markets, has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round co-led by White Star Capital and Innovation Endeavors , with participation from angel investors. The company plans to use the funding to speed up product development, expand its team, and support growth in global markets. Ben Choi | Christophe Bourque | Harpinder Singh | Olivier Babin | Naunidh Singh Bhalla 🔗 Read full article link in comment #Tetrix #ai #funding #startupnews #businessnews #businessupdate

Two years ago I joined Tetrix as the first full-time hire. No customers, no revenue, just an MVP and a vision. Today we announced our $15M Series A. Hard to believe how far we've come in two years, and we're just getting started!

🚀 Big news: Tetrix has raised a $15M Series A! 🚀 When we came out of stealth a little over a year and a half ago, we set out with one mission: to enable the free flow of information and capital in private markets. Alternative markets are a $20T+ asset class still running on 100 million PDFs. While public markets have benefited from decades of investment in data infrastructure and transparency, private markets have been left to wrestle with unstructured data, fragmented tools, and manual workflows. Tetrix changes that. By combining agentic workflows, AI-powered data normalization, and real-time analytics, we turn messy, unstructured fund data into clear, actionable insight — helping LPs uncover their biggest risks and find their best opportunities. The momentum since has been incredible: • $100B+ in AUM now managed on Tetrix • Clients across North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia — endowments, foundations, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, fund of funds, and family offices • 45-day analyst workflows collapsed into a single day, saving teams thousands of manual hours per investment This round is co-led by White Star Capital and Innovation Endeavors , who first backed us at the seed and have doubled down ever since, with participation from a phenomenal group of angel investors. We're deeply grateful for their conviction, and even more grateful to the clients who've trusted us and shaped the platform every step of the way. Here's our ask: 1. If you're (or know) an institutional investor or family office navigating private markets, we'd love to connect. 2. We're hiring across engineering, go-to-market, client strategy and operations, so if you know exceptional people, send them our way. Private markets have run on infrastructure built for the 1990s for far too long. Tetrix is building what comes next. Press release and exclusive coverage by Axios in the comments!

When I joined Adobe , I thought I'd stay for 2 years. Ten years later, I'm still here. Not because that was the plan. In fact, I never really had a plan. Like many young professionals, I thought my career would be a series of stepping stones. Join. Learn. Move. Repeat. Simple. But careers have a funny way of ignoring our timelines. Over the last decade, I've seen people leave for bigger opportunities. I've seen people return. I've seen technologies rise and fall. I've seen "critical" issues disappear and "small" projects change careers. Most importantly, I've seen how differently a career looks from the inside compared to the outside. When we're young, we imagine successful careers as straight lines. Promotion. Promotion. Promotion. Reality looks more like a maze. There are detours. Plateaus. Unexpected opportunities. And sometimes, the biggest growth happens during the periods when it feels like nothing is happening. Looking back, one lesson stands out. Experience isn't just about the number of years. It's about the number of patterns you've seen. The difficult customer. The impossible deadline. The failed project. The unexpected success. Over time, you realize that many "new" problems are actually old problems wearing different clothes. That's what experience gives you. Not all the answers. Just better questions. When I joined Adobe , I thought success would come from constantly looking ahead. Ten years later, I've learned that sometimes growth comes from staying long enough to understand what everyone else is rushing past. And that's a lesson I didn't expect to learn.

From San Jose to Munich, Armenia, Romania, France, and India — Adobe is welcoming 1,100+ interns and nearly 500 university graduates this year. The energy is incredible, and the work they're stepping into from day one is the real thing. Welcome, everyone. #AdobeLife
